source_messages.text: I'm starting a tiny document-outline utility. Everything lives in one module; each function takes a single JSON-style argument and returns a JSON-style value. The first piece, parse_heading, already works: it recognizes markdown heading lines (one to six '#' characters followed by one space) and returns the level plus the raw title text after that first space — it deliberately does not trim anything. Anything else gets None. Two standing decisions for everything we build here: (1) Titles stored in outlines, and therefore anything derived from them, must be stripped of surrounding whitespace. (2) Documents are messy — any line that is not a well-formed heading (plain prose, '#' with no following space, more than six '#', or a heading whose title is blank once stripped) is just content. Skip it quietly; never fail the whole parse over such a line.

request.text: Implement build_outline(lines). lines must be a list of strings; if it is not a list, or any element is not a string, return exactly {"error": "invalid input"}. Use parse_heading to recognize heading lines — don't re-implement that detection. Following the standing decisions, silently ignore every non-heading line and every heading whose title is empty once stripped, and store each node's title stripped of surrounding whitespace. Return the top-level nodes as a list in document order, each node shaped {"title": ..., "level": ..., "children": [...]}. Nesting rule: a heading becomes a child of the most recent heading with a strictly lower level; if there is no such heading, it is top-level. An empty input list yields [].

source_messages.text: The outline builder is in. Two things before the next piece. First, a forward-looking note: when we add the lookup tool later, I want query matching to ignore letter case — 'intro' should find 'Intro'. Second, the index. It walks an outline depth-first (a parent, then its children, then the next sibling) and numbers sections: top-level headings are "1", "2", and so on; children are "1.1", "1.2", joined with dots at every depth. One scope-limited policy: only headings of level 3 or less get index entries — level 4 and deeper, along with everything beneath them, are left out of the index entirely. That cutoff belongs to indexing only.

request.text: Implement index_sections(outline). outline is the node list produced by build_outline. Return a list of entries in depth-first pre-order, one entry {"number": ..., "title": ...} per included heading. Numbering: siblings count from 1 at each nesting level, joined with dots along the path (top level "1", its first child "1.1", that child's first child "1.1.1"). Include only headings whose level is 1, 2 or 3; skip any deeper node together with its whole subtree, per the indexing cutoff. If outline is not a list, or any visited node is not an object with a string "title", an integer "level" >= 1, and a list "children", return exactly {"error": "invalid outline"}. Extra keys on nodes are fine — ignore them. An empty outline yields [].

source_messages.text: Last piece now: the lookup. One correction to what I told you before — scrap the case-insensitive plan for queries. Matching must be case-sensitive after all: 'intro' must not match 'Intro'; only identical letter case counts.

request.text: Implement query_sections(request). request must be an object containing "outline" (the build_outline node list) and "text" (the query string). If request is not an object, or either key is missing, or text is not a non-empty string, return exactly {"error": "invalid query"}. Get the index by calling index_sections on the outline — reuse it, do not re-implement numbering — and if it returns its error object, pass that through unchanged as your result. A section matches when the query text occurs somewhere in its title with exactly matching letter case, per the corrected rule from my last message. Return {"matches": [...]} where each match is {"number": ..., "title": ...} in index order; when nothing matches, return {"matches": []}.

Now implementing build_outline(lines). Required: lines must be a list of strings; a non-list argument or any non-string element must produce exactly {"error": "invalid input"}. Each well-formed heading with a non-blank stripped title becomes a node {"title", "level", "children"}; a heading nests under the most recent heading with a strictly lower level, otherwise it is top-level; document order is preserved; an empty list yields []. Standing rules (required, global): (R-STRIP) every stored title is stripped of surrounding whitespace; (R-IGNORE-BAD) any line that is not a well-formed heading — plain prose, '#' without a following space, seven or more '#', or a title that is blank once stripped — is silently skipped as content and must never cause an error.

effective_rules.text: Titles stored in outline nodes — and therefore in everything derived from them — are stripped of surrounding whitespace.

Any line that is not a well-formed heading (missing space after the hashes, more than six hashes, blank title after stripping, plain prose) is treated as content and skipped silently; it never makes parsing fail.
